s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive painful skin lesions and ulcers with systemic symptoms and laboratory abnormalities
salient_findings: Progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
Enlargement of the tongue with difficulty in mastication
Numbness of the distal lower limbs without weakness
Circinate purpuric patches with erosions on the skin
Hemorrhagic flaccid bullae on the posterior perineum
Low serum zinc level
Subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and eosinophilic bands on biopsy
key_facts: 1-week history of progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
3-month history of tongue enlargement leading to difficulty with mastication
3-month history of numbness of the distal lower limbs without weakness
Patient has IgG λ-type multiple myeloma
Patient has anemia and lytic lesions in the calvarium
Patient is taking folic acid and intramuscular cyanocobalamin supplements
Platelet count is 171 × 10^3/μL
Prothrombin time is 11.7 seconds
Activated partial thromboplastin time is 36.0 seconds
Serum zinc level is 34.4 μg/dL
Biopsy from left groin showed subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate
Direct immunofluorescence test was negative
Herpes simplex virus PCR from perineal ulcer swab was negative

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of progressive, painful blisters and ulcers, along with a history of tongue enlargement, numbness of the distal lower limbs, and a diagnosis of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma, aligns with the characteristic symptoms of POEMS syndrome, which includes polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, monoclonal gammopathy, and skin changes.

rejected.label: bullous pemphigoid
rejected.why: The negative direct immunofluorescence test and the presence of subepidermal blisters with chronic inflammatory infiltrate do not strongly support bullous pemphigoid, which typically has positive immunofluorescence findings.

rejected.label: ulcer
rejected.why: Ulcer is too nonspecific and does not account for the full spectrum of the patient's symptoms, including the neurological and hematological findings.

rejected.label: vasculitis
rejected.why: The biopsy findings and laboratory results do not specifically indicate vasculitis, which would typically involve inflammation of the blood vessel walls.

rejected.label: pyoderma gangrenosum
rejected.why: While pyoderma gangrenosum can cause ulcers, the patient's overall clinical picture, including the monoclonal gammopathy and neuropathy, is more consistent with POEMS syndrome.
